title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-scratchpad-2
content:
Context:
- Working notes for ongoing thrash/warmup incident hitting dedicated GPU pools (JIRA-INF-784).
- Symptoms: repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles (capacity thrash) during traffic bursts; cold-start token latency spikes (~3x) for some model variants; warmup tasks failing intermittently.

Timeline + quick hits:
- 2024-09-29 18:12 UTC: Pager triggered; observed 503s and pod restarts for pool-23 (p100 nodes).
- 2024-09-29 18:20 UTC: Canary opts rolled back to previous rollout; partial relief ~10m.
- 2024-09-29 18:45 UTC: Autoscaler initiated 6 scale-ups then 5 scale-downs in ~12m window.

Commands / logs I pulled (snippets):
- kubectl get hpa -n dedicated-pool
  NAME            REFERENCE            TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
  pool-23-hpa     Deployment/pool-23    60%/80%   1         12        8          4h

- kubectl describe pod pool-23-warmup-0 -n dedicated-pool
  Events:
    Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
    ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
    Normal  Scheduled  3m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ...
    Warning Failed     2m    kubelet            Error: failed to start container

- tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/warmup.log | sed -n '1,120p'
  [2024-09-29T18:17:05Z] warmup: starting warmup for model: redwood-base-v2
  [2024-09-29T18:17:07Z] warmup: kv-cache miss for prefix, triggering full load
  [2024-09-29T18:17:08Z] warmup: OOM while pinning cache entry (alloc 1.2G)
  [2024-09-29T18:17:08Z] warmup: aborting warmup; marking pod unhealthy

- kubectl logs deployment/pool-23-scheduler -n infra | grep "scale" -n
  234: INFO 2024-09-29T18:16:42Z scale: evaluating policy (latency-weighted)
  236: INFO 2024-09-29T18:16:43Z scale: predicted need=6 nodes (current=2, max=12)
  241: INFO 2024-09-29T18:17:10Z scale: launching 4 nodes for pool-23
  259: WARN 2024-09-29T18:19:25Z scale: observed 80% of launched nodes failed health checks (warmup)

- gcloud compute instances tail-serial-port-logs for failed instances:
  2024-09-29T18:17:05 Startup-script: pulling docker image redwood/serve:stable
  2024-09-29T18:17:35 Startup-script: gpu-drivers ready
  2024-09-29T18:18:02 Startup-script: runtime service failed to bind to device: device busy

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Warmup tasks allocate large KV cache entries that exceed per-GPU memory reservation -> OOM during warmup -> node marked unhealthy -> autoscaler removes node -> thrash.
- H2: Autoscaler launches N nodes; warmup controller starts heavy concurrent loads on all new nodes -> temporary global memory pressure and OOMs.
- H3: Device/driver init race: runtime cannot bind to GPU because device plugin/driver not ready -> readiness probe times out -> false negative health.
- H4: Model-variant mismatch: some variants need more memory for warmup than inference; autoscaler not variant-aware when selecting node type.

Evidence mapping:
- OOM lines in warmup.log -> supports H1 (reproduced on multiple nodes).
- scheduler logs: "80% launched nodes failed health checks (warmup)" -> supports H1/H2.
- instance startup logs with "device busy" -> supports H3.

Short-term mitigations tried and outcomes:
- Reduced warmup concurrency (8 -> 2): fewer per-node OOMs but overall warmup time increased; autoscaler still scaled down before warmup finished (partial).
- Increased health-check timeout (60s -> 180s): fewer false negatives but longer degraded windows and higher cost.
- Pin warmup path to quantized smaller-ram variant for redwood-base-v2: stopped most OOMs for that model, but customer-large models still fail.

Proposed longer-term fixes:
- Warmup orchestration: sequentialize heavy-model warmups across new nodes (leader election per-launch-group).
- Gated scale-down: autoscaler should wait for warmup-complete signal (e.g., kv-cache coverage > threshold) before removing nodes.
- Variant-aware scheduling: autoscaler to consult warmup memory profiles when choosing node type / reservations.
- Startup order hardening: ensure driver/runtime bind before node is marked Ready; add retries/backoff for device allocation.

Action items (owners):
- [ ] Add warmup metrics (kv-cache pins, warmup-memory-used) -> EPIC INF-WARMUP-METRICS (Maya).
- [ ] Add autoscaler gating on warmup-complete (feature-flagged PR opened) -> PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412 (Ravi/Maya).
- [ ] Reproduce device busy race in smaller cluster; capture driver/kernel versions (Ethan).
- [ ] Run controlled repro (8 nodes) with synthetic warmup workload and capture timelines (Ravi).

Instrumentation checklist for next repro:
- GPU memory allocation timeline (per-node, timestamped)
- Warmup controller: prefixes requested, per-model estimate vs actual memory
- Scheduler: policy inputs for scale decisions
- Kubelet/device-plugin logs and container runtime start events

Open questions:
- Are particular GPU driver/kernel versions correlated with "device busy" errors? Need a version matrix.
- Any concurrent system jobs at that time (kernel updates, backups) that could collide with startup?
- Can we implement a cheap warmup probe (small prefix hit) to mark node warm before full KV load?

Slack/JIRA breadcrumbs:
- infra-ops thread: "saw 5 nodes fail warmup in the same minute, looked like OOMs while loading LLM cache"
- JIRA-INF-784: incident report (30% request error rate for ~12m)

Plan / next steps:
- Today: run controlled repro with reduced concurrency and capture detailed logs.
- Next: push gating change to autoscaler behind feature flag to hold scale-down until warmup completes.
- Follow-up: design variant-aware scheduling and cost model tradeoffs (warmup time vs overprovisioning).

Notes: saving as a scratchpad; will extract a cleaner timeline and post-mortem after repro + short-term fixes validated.

-- Ravi
